Timeline::days_between¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

std::int64_t Timeline::days_between(const Timeline& other) const

Count Complete Elapsed 24-Hour Units¶

days_between() subtracts two scalar instants and returns the signed number of complete 24-hour units from the receiver to other. One day is exactly 86,400,000,000,000 nanoseconds. The quotient truncates toward zero, so an interval of 47 hours returns 1, while -47 hours returns -1.

This is deliberately different from add_days(), which moves to the same local clock on another calendar date. A civil day can contain 23, 24, or 25 elapsed hours when a timezone offset changes. Use days_between() for elapsed-duration thresholds; use calendar operations when date labels are the governing concept.

Example: Incomplete Units Are Discarded¶

const auto start = pluss::timeline::make("2024-01-01T00:00:00Z");
const auto end = pluss::timeline::make("2024-01-02T02:03:04.500000000Z");

std::cout << start.days_between(end) << '\n'
          << end.days_between(start) << '\n';

Output¶

1
-1

The remaining two hours, three minutes, four seconds, and 500 milliseconds do not round the answer away from zero. Reverse order changes only the sign.

Example: A Civil Day Across Spring DST Is Only 23 Hours¶

const auto before = pluss::timeline::make("2024-03-09T10:30:00Z")
                        .tz_convert("America/Edmonton");
const auto next_civil_day = before.add_days(1);

std::cout << "hours=" << before.hours_between(next_civil_day) << '\n'
          << "days=" << before.days_between(next_civil_day) << '\n'
          << "after_24_hours="
          << before.days_between(before.add_hours(24)) << '\n';

Output¶

hours=23
days=0
after_24_hours=1

The first endpoint is the next local date at the same clock time, but the spring transition removes one elapsed hour. It therefore has not completed an elapsed 24-hour unit.

Example: Non-Scalar And NaT Inputs Are Rejected¶

const auto start = pluss::timeline::make("2024-01-01T00:00:00Z");

for (const auto& other : {
         pluss::timeline::make(""),
         pluss::timeline::make({"2024-01-01", "2024-01-02"}),
     }) {
  try {
    (void)start.days_between(other);
  } catch (const pluss::Error&) {
    std::cout << "rejected\n";
  }
}

Output¶

rejected
rejected

Both operands must be scalar defined instants. Timezone names need not match for elapsed methods because epoch subtraction is independent of presentation zone. The implementation uses widened subtraction, so opposite ends of the valid epoch-nanosecond range cannot overflow before division.
